info.bio:
Eddy Arnold, nacido el 15 de mayo de 1918 en la localidad de Henderson, condado de Chester, Tennessee y fallecido el 8 de mayo de 2008 en Franklin, condado de Williamson, Tennessee debido a una enfermedad, fue un músico estadounidense, especialmente volcado a la música country, cuyo verdadero nombre era Richard Edward Arnold.

Entre su debut en el mundo de la música en 1945 y 1954, Eddie logró 58 top ten consecutivos, y nunca marcó menos de un top 40 durante sus 21 años de carrera

scenes.name: El pop en televisión: Ready Steady Go! y Top of the Pops
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: A principios de 1966 había tres programas pop. Top of the Pops (BBC1) presentaba la lista tal cual, de Eddy Arnold a los Stones; A Whole Scene Going (BBC2), con Barry Fantoni y Wendy Varnals, era más reflexivo. El mejor era Ready Steady Go! (agosto de 1963-1966), que traducía al televisor el ritmo de la cultura juvenil: actuaciones en directo entre el público, mujeres como presentadoras, productoras y artistas (Vicki Wickham, Cathy McGowan), visitantes de Tamla y del soul, y la cámara de Michael Lindsay-Hogg pegada a Jagger y a las bailarinas mod de falda corta. En agosto de 1965 el público invadió el plató mientras los Stones tocaban «Satisfaction».

podcast.title: Firing of Tom Parker (1953)
podcast.body: Arnold fired Colonel Parker in 1953 after discovering that Parker was forming a tour for other RCA acts, led by Hank Snow, which violated their exclusive management agreement. "In 1953, Arnold found out that Parker was putting together a tour of other RCA acts, headed by Hank Snow. Arnold fired the Kernel."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: $50,000 Severance Payment to Parker
podcast.body: Upon being fired, Tom Parker insisted on and received a $50,000 severance package from Arnold, citing the substantial earnings Arnold was making from contracts Parker had negotiated. "He insisted on Arnold giving him a severance package of $50,000, because of how much money Arnold was making from the contracts that Parker had negotiated for him."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Admiration for Jean Austin
podcast.body: Arnold was a fan of Jean Austin, which made him eager to connect with Tom Parker. "Arnold was a fan of Jean Austin, and so eagerly linked up with Parker."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Early Career with Pee Wee King's Golden West Cowboys
podcast.body: Eddie Arnold began his career as a young singer working with Pee Wee King's Golden West Cowboys. "Eddie Arnold, a young singer who was then working with Pee Wee Kings, Golden West Cowboys."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: KRAK Radio Station Staple
podcast.body: Eddie Arnold was considered a staple artist on KRAK, a country and western radio station managed by Allan Torbert. He represented the type of performer that would satisfy country music purists. "Eddie Arnold, Buck Owens, Porter Wagner. I mean, these were KRAK staples."

podcast.title: Kickbacks and Financial Arrangements
podcast.body: Both Steve Scholls and Eddie Arnold received money from Hill and Range for Arnold recording their published songs. Parker exploited Scholls's involvement in kickbacks to control him and took 25% of a $20,000 bribe Hill and Range paid Arnold. "Both Scholls and Arnold were given money by Hill and Range, for Arnold recording the publisher's songs. Parker had Scholls in his pocket, because he knew that Scholls was taking kickbacks, and could inform Scholls as buses at RCA, and Parker in turn took 25% of the $20,000 bribe the Till and Range paid Arnold."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Parker's Management Team for Arnold
podcast.body: Tom Parker managed Arnold, Steve Scholls (head of country and R&B at RCA) handled record production, Hill and Range music publishers managed song performance and publication (with kickbacks), and the William Morris Agency handled bookings. "Parker would handle the management. Steve Scholls, the head of country and Arvin B at RCA, would handle the record production."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Rise to Stardom with Parker's Team
podcast.body: Arnold became one of the biggest stars in country music, a success largely attributed to the management team Tom Parker assembled around him. "Eddie Arnold was to go on to become one of the biggest stars in country music, and that was in large part because of the team that Tom Parker built around him."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Signing with RCA Records
podcast.body: Tom Parker quickly secured a deal for Eddie Arnold to sign with RCA Records as a solo artist. "Parker quickly got Arnold signed to RCA Records as a solo artist."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
